headline: Approved memo streamlining event permitting and public-space activation, and memo on Burlington Forward parks and homelessness recommendations, both unanimously.
summary: The meeting covered a playground replacement program for Ethan Allen Park, Smalley Park, and Baird Park, plus early planning for a larger Leddy Park destination playground. decision_titles: Streamlining events and activating public spaces memo
plain_text:
PARKS, ARTS & CULTURE COMMITTEE 
Meeting Minutes – October 20, 206 
(Draft) 
Call to Order 
Chair Councilor Schachter called the meeting to order at 12:02 PM. 
Approval of Agenda and Minutes 
• The agenda was approved by unanimous vote. 
• The minutes from the previous meeting were approved by unanimous vote. 
Public Forum 
Moran/Frame Activation and Community Programming 
A member of the public and representative of Friends of the Frame spoke regarding activation of the 
Moran Plant/Frame area. The speaker discussed previous partnerships among community organizations, 
Burlington City Arts (BCA), CEDO, and city departments to host public events and cultural programming. 
Key points included: 
• Support for increased programming and public activation of the space. 
• Interest in clarifying management and permitting responsibilities for the site. 
• Desire to revive previous collaborative efforts among nonprofit organizations and city partners. 
• Support for accessibility improvements, including ADA infrastructure and amenities that would 
encourage broader public use. 
Committee members thanked the speaker and encouraged continued dialogue with city staff regarding 
future programming opportunities. 
Burlington Forward Comments 
A member of the public encouraged the committee to review recommendations and comments 
previously submitted by the Racial Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (REIB) Board concerning sections of 
Burlington Forward under committee review. 
Committee Process and Public Engagement 
Councilor Melo Grant spoke during public forum regarding public concerns about committee processes 
and communication among elected officials. Councilor Grant emphasized: 
• The importance of improved coordination among councilors. 
• Increased transparency and communication with the public. 
• Opportunities for greater collaboration between committee leadership and council leadership.
Public forum was closed at approximately 12:12 PM. 
 
1. Parks Department Update: Playground Replacement Program 
Presentation by Sophie Sabo, Parks Planning Division Director 
Sophia (Sophie) Sauve, Director of Parks Planning, Design and Construction, provided an overview of 
Burlington's playground replacement program and upcoming public engagement efforts. 
Key points included: 
Existing Conditions 
• Many city playgrounds were installed during the same era and are reaching the end of their 
useful lives simultaneously. 
• Aging equipment presents maintenance, safety, and accessibility challenges. 
• Several playgrounds have already required partial or complete removal due to deterioration. 
Partnership with the Parks Foundation 
• The Burlington Parks Foundation has committed to raising approximately $150,000 annually to 
support playground replacement projects. 
• City funding through Penny for Parks contributes approximately $100,000 annually toward 
replacements. 
• The partnership prioritizes playgrounds that incorporate universal design principles and 
improved accessibility. 
Accessibility and Universal Design 
Future playgrounds will: 
• Include accessible surfacing and pathways. 
• Improve access for individuals using mobility devices and families with strollers. 
• Incorporate play opportunities for children of varying abilities. 
• Include sensory, tactile, and quiet play elements. 
• Create opportunities for multigenerational use and participation. 
Upcoming Playground Replacements 
Three playground replacement projects are planned: 
• Ethan Allen Park 
• Smalley Park
• Baird Park 
Staff reported that replacing multiple playgrounds through a coordinated procurement process is 
expected to improve efficiency and reduce costs. 
Public Engagement Process 
The Parks Department has: 
• Conducted tabling events at each park. 
• Distributed multilingual public surveys. 
• Begun outreach to local schools. 
• Sought input from caregivers, grandparents, teens, and other community members regarding 
desired amenities. 
Leddy Park Destination Playground 
Staff also reported early planning efforts for a larger destination playground at Leddy Park. The project is 
expected to require additional design work and external grant funding. 
Committee Discussion 
Councilor McKnight expressed appreciation for the project and emphasized the importance of 
playgrounds as community assets. 
Questions were raised regarding: 
• Procurement processes for playground vendors. 
• Opportunities to streamline future replacement efforts. 
• Funding adequacy and long-term sustainability. 
Staff noted that while current funding appears sufficient for neighborhood-scale projects, construction 
costs continue to increase and additional grant funding will likely be necessary for larger facilities such 
as Leddy Park. 
Committee members also discussed opportunities to support public engagement efforts and promote 
participation in surveys and outreach activities. 
 
2. Draft Memo: Streamlining Events and Activating Public Spaces 
The committee continued discussion of a draft memorandum regarding city event permitting, public-
space activation, and support for outside organizations hosting events on public property. 
Background 
Councilor Schachter noted that the memo originated from budget discussions and broader concerns 
regarding the complexity of organizing events in Burlington parks and public spaces.
The committee reviewed recommendations aimed at: 
• Improving coordination among city departments. 
• Reducing barriers for community organizations. 
• Clarifying permitting processes. 
• Supporting activation of public spaces throughout the city. 
City Staff Feedback 
Event Coordination Function 
CAO Katherine Schad reported that an interdepartmental working group representing approximately 
nine departments has been meeting regularly regarding event coordination. 
Staff generally supported the recommendations but suggested revising the recommendation for an 
"event shepherd" to allow flexibility in implementation. 
Rather than assigning responsibility to a single individual, staff recommended language allowing for: 
• A staff lead, 
• A coordinated committee, or 
• A dedicated office. 
Centralized Event Services 
Staff supported continued exploration of a more centralized event coordination model and noted that 
additional planning and resources would likely be necessary. 
Technology and Permitting 
Staff expressed support for efforts to: 
• Improve OpenGov functionality. 
• Enhance user experience. 
• Simplify application and review processes. 
Vendor Regulations 
Director Kara Alnasrawi clarified that the Church Street Marketplace Commission maintains separate 
authority over permitting and regulations within Marketplace boundaries. 
Security Requirements 
Committee members discussed language related to event security requirements. 
Staff clarified: 
• Event organizers are responsible for security expenses associated with private events.
• Certain events may require police or fire personnel depending on size and operational needs. 
• The city does not routinely provide security for non-city-sponsored events. 
Following discussion, committee members agreed that the security recommendation could create 
confusion and proposed removing it from the memo. 
Motion 
Councilor Schachter moved to approve the memorandum with two amendments: 
1. Revise the event coordination recommendation to refer to a "staff person, committee, or 
office." 
2. Remove the recommendation related to event security. 
Councilor McKnight seconded. 
Motion passed unanimously. 
 
3. Draft Memo: Burlington Forward Recommendations 
The committee discussed a second memorandum addressing sections of Burlington Forward relevant to 
parks, public lands, and homelessness response strategies. 
Discussion 
Councilor Schachter explained that the memo focused on areas where PAC has direct expertise or 
responsibilities. 
Particular discussion centered on recommendations related to: 
• Public lands policies, 
• Homelessness response, 
• Potential consideration of sanctioned camping models. 
Committee members emphasized the need for: 
• Additional legal review from the City Attorney's Office. 
• Broader community engagement. 
• Examination of approaches used by other municipalities. 
Public Comment 
A member of the public suggested that, in addition to legal review, future discussions should include: 
• Service providers, 
• Subject matter experts,
• Individuals with lived experience, 
• Representatives from other municipalities that have explored similar approaches. 
Councilor McKnight expressed support for broader discussion while emphasizing that sanctioned 
camping should not be viewed as the sole strategy for addressing homelessness. 
Motion 
Councilor Schachter moved to approve the memorandum with amended language requesting future 
work sessions involving: 
• Individuals with lived experience, 
• Service providers, 
• Municipal representatives, 
• Experts on homelessness response and housing strategies. 
Councilor McKnight seconded. 
Motion passed unanimously. 
 
Adjournment 
The meeting adjourned at 1:02 PM.
